newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa up at mid-day, crosses active.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa up at mid-day, crosses active.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa rose in light morning trade as the pound weakened on Monday and traders said a large cross on December accounted for most of the volume.
The market opened mixed on the back of New York but rose on sterling weakness, traders said.
Active December, which last week tested support several times at 1,030, ended the session eight stg up at 1,039 after opening four stg down at 1,027.
A large cross of 1,100 lots on December accounted for most of the December volume of 1,528 lots, traders said. Total volume was 2,366.
Nearby March also rose eight stg to 1,062 and September was up seven stg at 1,009.
"The only support has been sterling. It has been a bit lower this morning and this bolstered the volume in London," a trader said.
However, traders believed the market had bottomed out and was ready to start moving up.
"The market feels based out and want to go higher," one said.
No new word on crop estimates was likely to reach the market until the end of August, he added.
Earlier, technical analysts said cocoa was likely to drift lower with December moving towards nearby support at 1,020 stg.
